subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 11
intro: Edexcel Higher style. No calculator. Section A is Number, Section B is Algebra. Show your working in the working box: method marks count even if the final answer slips. Before you divide, ask: is the number I'm dividing by bigger or smaller than 1? Type powers with ^ (for example x^2).

questions.q:
Section A: Number
Without working them out, which calculation gives an answer bigger than 36?
questions.ms: 36 ÷ 0.8 = 45. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer bigger. The others are 28.8, 30 and 34.2, all smaller than 36.

questions.q: Work out an estimate for the value of 21.3 × 5.920.208
questions.ms: 600. M1 round each number to 1 s.f.: 20, 6, 0.2. M1 20 × 6 = 120. A1 120 ÷ 0.2 = 600 (dividing by 0.2 is the same as multiplying by 5).

questions.q:
Omar works out 63 ÷ 0.7 and gets the answer 9.
Explain why Omar's answer must be wrong, and work out the correct answer.
questions.ms: B1 0.7 is less than 1, so the answer must be bigger than 63 (Omar's answer is smaller). B1 90 (630 ÷ 7 = 90).

questions.q:
You are given that 238 × 56 = 13 328.
Work out 13 328 ÷ 5.6
questions.ms: 2380. 13 328 ÷ 56 = 238, and 5.6 is 10 times smaller than 56, so the answer is 10 times bigger.
56. Both numbers are 100 times smaller than in 13 328 ÷ 238, so the answer stays 56.

questions.q: Work out (−3)<sup>2</sup> − 4 × (−2)<sup>3</sup>
Round 0.003 0049 to 3 significant figures.
questions.ms: 0.00300. The first significant figure is the 3; the next two are 0 and 0, and the 4 after them means round down. The zeros must stay to show 3 s.f.

questions.q: Write 540 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
questions.ms: 2² × 3³ × 5. M1 a correct factor tree or repeated division, A1 index form.

questions.q: Find the smallest whole number you can multiply 540 by to make a square number.
questions.ms: 15. M1 need every power even: 2² × 3⁴ × 5², so multiply by 3 × 5, A1 15 (540 × 15 = 8100 = 90²).

questions.q: Solve 27n ÷ 3 = 94
questions.ms: n = 3. M1 write everything as powers of 3: 27ⁿ = 3³ⁿ and 9⁴ = 3⁸, M1 3³ⁿ ÷ 3¹ = 3³ⁿ⁻¹ so 3n − 1 = 8, A1 n = 3.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length √72 cm and width √18 cm.
Work out the perimeter of the rectangle. Give your answer in the form a√2
questions.ms: 18√2 cm. M1 √72 = √36 × √2 = 6√2 and √18 = √9 × √2 = 3√2, M1 2 × (6√2 + 3√2), A1 18√2. Simplify each surd first; don't add under the root.

questions.q:
Section B: Algebra
Work out the value of 3(5 − c) when c = −4
Fully factorise 15p2 − 20p
questions.ms: 5p(3p − 4). Take out the highest common factor of 15p² and 20p, which is 5p. 5(3p² − 4p) and p(15p − 20) are only partly factorised.

questions.q: Factorise fully 12x2 − 18x
questions.ms: 6x(2x − 3). B2 fully correct; B1 partly factorised, e.g. 6(2x² − 3x), 3x(4x − 6) or x(12x − 18).
x = 5. M1 expand: 8x − 12 = 3x + 13, M1 collect: 5x = 25, A1 x = 5.
x = 4. M1 add 3x to both sides: 9 = 8x − 23, M1 add 23: 32 = 8x, A1 x = 4.

questions.q: Solve 7 − x3 = x + 1
questions.ms: x = 1. M1 multiply both sides by 3: 7 − x = 3(x + 1), M1 7 − x = 3x + 3 so 4 = 4x, A1 x = 1.

questions.q:
The sides of a triangle are (x + 5) cm, (2x − 1) cm and 3x cm. The perimeter is 40 cm.
Form and solve an equation to find x. Then work out the length of the longest side.
questions.ms: 18 cm. M1 x + 5 + 2x − 1 + 3x = 40, M1 6x + 4 = 40, A1 x = 6, A1 sides are 11, 11 and 18, so the longest is 18 cm.

questions.q: Make a the subject of the formula a3 − 4 = 2b
questions.ms: a = 6b + 12. M1 add 4: a/3 = 2b + 4, A1 multiply by 3: a = 3(2b + 4) = 6b + 12.

questions.q: Make x the subject of the formula y = 3x − 52
questions.hint: Type a fraction with brackets and /, like (y + 1)/4
questions.ms: x = (2y + 5)/3. M1 multiply by 2 then add 5: 3x = 2y + 5, A1 divide by 3: x = (2y + 5)/3.

questions.q: Simplify 4x5y2 × 3x2y
questions.ms: 12x⁷y³. Multiply the numbers (4 × 3), add the powers of each letter (x⁵⁺², y²⁺¹).

questions.q: Simplify (3a2b4)3
questions.ms: 27a⁶b¹². M1 3³ = 27, A1 multiply each power by 3: a⁶b¹². (9a⁶b¹² cubes the letters but not the 3.)

questions.q:
Here are the first four terms of an arithmetic sequence.
5, 11, 17, 23, …
Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term.
questions.ms: 6n − 1. M1 the common difference is 6, so 6n, A1 6 × 1 = 6 and the first term is 5, so subtract 1.

questions.q: Is 150 a term in the sequence 5, 11, 17, 23, …? You must give a reason.
questions.ms: No. M1 6n − 1 = 150 gives 6n = 151, A1 n = 25.17 is not a whole number (or: the terms are all one less than a multiple of 6; 149 and 155 are terms, 150 is not).

questions.q: Which of these is a geometric sequence?
questions.ms: 2, 6, 18, 54: each term is multiplied by 3. An arithmetic sequence adds the same number each time; 1, 4, 9, 16 are square numbers; 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 is Fibonacci.
